case.title: Churchill Onyeka Ibeagwa v. XL Logistics Limited (Subsidiary of XL Management Services Ltd)
defendants: XL Logistics Limited (Subsidiary of XL Management Services Ltd)

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Claimant filed suit NICN/LA/98/2013 on 26th February 2013 seeking payment of salaries, declaration that suspension is wrongful, and damages.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Ruling on whether the suit is statute-barred.

material_facts: Claimant's employment with defendant was determined or he was suspended indefinitely.
Claimant's salaries were allegedly unpaid from February 2005.
Claimant wrote letters through his solicitor to the defendant.

chronology.event: Cause of action arose (salaries due for payment).
Claimant filed suit at National Industrial Court.

facts.employment_relationship: Claimant was an employee of the defendant.
facts.contractual_relationship: Employment contract between claimant and defendant.

claims.claim: Payment of salaries from February 2005 till judgment.
Declaration that the purported indefinite suspension is wrongful, unlawful, in breach of right to fair hearing, breach of contract, null, void and of no effect.
N5,000,000 damages for untold hardship and torture occasioned by breach of contract.

reliefs_sought.relief: Payment of salaries from February 2005 till judgment.
Payment of salaries as a subsisting staff or as a staff whose employment has been determined.
Declaration that the purported indefinite suspension is wrongful, unlawful, in breach of right to fair hearing, breach of contract, null, void and of no effect.
N5,000,000 damages for untold hardship and torture occasioned by breach of contract.

questions_of_law: Whether the cause of action arose in February 2005.
Whether the suit filed on 26th February 2013 is statute-barred under the Lagos State Limitation Law.

claimant_arguments: The letter of suspension indicated that the defendant will communicate to him, which it did not.
Two letters were written by his solicitor to the defendant.

party_authorities.proposition: Where claim is for payment of salaries wrongfully withheld, cause of action accrues from date salaries are due; liability does not depend on demand.

findings_of_fact.finding: Cause of action arose in February 2005.

findings_of_law.finding: Lagos State Limitation Law Cap. L67 Laws of Lagos State 2003 section 8 provides for 6 years limitation for actions such as the instant case.
The suit is statute-barred as it was filed 8 years after the cause of action arose.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The cause of action arose in February 2005 when salaries were due. The suit was filed on 26th February 2013, more than 6 years after the cause of action arose. The Lagos State Limitation Law provides a 6-year limitation period. The claimant's arguments regarding the suspension letter and solicitor's letters do not affect the running of time. Therefore, the suit is statute-barred.

arguments.claimant: The suspension letter indicated communication would be made; solicitor wrote letters to defendant.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The cause of action arose in February 2005. The suit was filed on 26th February 2013, 8 years later. The applicable limitation period is 6 years under the Lagos State Limitation Law. The claimant's arguments do not stop time from running.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A cause of action for wrongful withholding of salaries accrues from the date the salaries are due for payment. An action filed more than 6 years after the cause of action arose is statute-barred under the Lagos State Limitation Law.

ratio_decidendi.principle: A cause of action for wrongful withholding of salaries accrues from the date the salaries are due for payment. An action filed more than 6 years after the cause of action arose is statute-barred under the Lagos State Limitation Law.
ratio_decidendi.application: The cause of action arose in February 2005. The suit was filed on 26th February 2013, more than 6 years later. Therefore, the suit is statute-barred.

legal_principles.principle: Cause of action for wrongful withholding of salaries accrues from the date the salaries are due for payment.
Liability of employer for unpaid salaries does not generally depend on demand for payment.
